digest.intro: Infrastructure cracks, geopolitical pivots, and materials that disorder on purpose.

items.title: Trump-Xi-Putin trilateral set for APEC sidelines in Shenzhen
items.blurb: A three-way summit on nuclear nonproliferation between the U.S., China, and Russia would be the first of its kind since the Cold War ended — not a photo op but a structural signal about who the great powers think they are dealing with. The choice of Shenzhen as venue is itself a message.

items.title: Silicon Valley lashed itself to Trump before the midterms. Now what?
items.blurb: Altman, Musk, Zuckerberg — the people whose entire brand is seeing around corners — gathered at the White House five weeks before a midterm wave went against them and signed on to a 'Super Intelligence' agenda. The Tech Review piece treats it correctly: not as a politics story but as a prestige and judgment story about a class that monetizes future-prediction and just catastrophically misfired on the most legible near-term event available.

items.title: FAA deployed AI system-wide, then the analog infrastructure collapsed
items.blurb: Only the third nationwide ground stop in FAA history — 4.5 hours, over a million travelers affected, Air Canada cancelling all U.S. flights — triggered by decades-old analog telecom equipment, days after the agency expanded its $875M AI routing system to all 22 national airspace centers. The union representing air traffic controllers wasn't involved in designing or testing that AI system, which is the detail that should follow you: AI recommendations layered on top of infrastructure the Secretary of Transportation himself says cannot compete with 21st-century demands.

items.title: Nvidia allegedly funded AI startups to buy its own GPUs and inflate demand
items.blurb: The allegation, earning 930 points on HN, is structurally Enron: Nvidia investing in startups whose primary activity was purchasing Nvidia GPUs, thereby manufacturing the demand signal that justified the valuation. If the mechanism holds up, it's the cleanest demand-fabrication scheme in modern tech — and it explains a lot about why the GPU shortage felt engineered.

items.title: Disorder is a feature: MIT's scale-rich metamaterials built from network topology
items.blurb: Published in Nature this week: instead of repeating unit cells, MIT and Northeastern built metamaterials from support beams of varying sizes arranged like a leaf's vasculature or a dragonfly's wing venation — deliberately disordered, like a real network. The resulting materials outperform conventional ordered metamaterials on sudden-impact absorption and can function as acoustic lenses, with stiffness tunable across a wide range. The core idea — that controlled disorder beats perfect periodicity — is the kind of principle that migrates into generative design fast.

items.title: All 13 versions of Monkey Island, side by side
items.blurb: Someone built a WebGL-rendered interactive archive of the same 12 moments from Monkey Island across every version ever released — EGA, CGA, Mac, FM Towns, Atari ST mono, all aspect-corrected to 4:3 with period-accurate CRT shader presets ported from DOSBox. The concept is exactly right: fix the moment, change the machine. It's visual archaeology and interface history and a meditation on how rendering technology shapes emotional register, all in one draggable window.

items.title: Robin Sloan: software is now distributed as essays that execute
items.blurb: Sloan points at the gap between the PyTorch configurator grid (old distribution: select your options, copy a command) and the new pattern where you copy a prompt, tune it with a little matrix of toggles, and paste it into an AI thread that installs and configures the software for you. His frame: the .dmg and .msi have been superseded by the postcard. The piece is short and the observation is genuinely weird in the right way.

items.title: Jonathan Blow — If AI solved coding, why is my software still the same?
items.blurb: Blow is one of the few people treating software quality as a craft and civilization problem rather than a velocity metric. This talk asks the precise question you'd want asked right now: if AI is transforming programming, where is the evidence in the actual software we use? 432 HN points suggests it lands.

facts.fact: The FAA's AI routing system — SMART — rerouted 180 flights and saved an average of 80 gallons of fuel per flight in its Washington D.C. pilot, then went live across all 22 national airspace centers days before the analog backbone caused only the third nationwide ground stop in FAA history.

MIT's new scale-rich metamaterials are designed not from repeating unit cells but from networks of beams with varying sizes inspired by leaf vasculature and dragonfly wing venation — the disorder itself is what gives them superior impact absorption.

The Monkey Island side-by-side archive captures every screen in ScummVM with 4:3 aspect correction and CRT shader presets ported from DOSBox Staging, rendering each version on the monitor type closest to its original hardware — including a Hercules mono version using only the middle 640 of its 720 columns.

art_picks.title: Sans Soleil
art_picks.creator: Chris Marker
art_picks.why: A meditation on memory, travel, ritual, and how images shape (and fail to capture) culture — Marker treats the camera as an instrument for excavating invisible social systems across Japan and Guinea-Bissau. The form IS the argument: an essay film that refuses to separate the aesthetic from the anthropological. If you haven't seen it, it'll reorganize how you think about documentation and time.

art_picks.title: Selected Ambient Works Volume II
art_picks.creator: Aphex Twin
art_picks.why: Not background music — a system for inducing specific interior states through pure texture and interval. Aphex built a sensory architecture out of near-silence; the craft is in what's withheld. Pairs absurdly well with generative work sessions where you want to lower the threshold between thinking and making.

art_picks.title: Mycelium Networks (ongoing research & installation practice)
art_picks.creator: Neri Oxman
art_picks.why: Oxman's work sits exactly at the edge you care about: biological process as formal language, nature as design system, the body of the object as computation. Her 'Material Ecology' framework treats software, fabrication, and organism as one continuous medium — genuinely new aesthetic territory, not just bio-inspired décor.

events.name: Hard Art — MoMA PS1
events.venue: MoMA PS1, 22-25 Jackson Ave, Long Island City, Queens
events.why: A major survey of abstract painting by Black artists from 1969 to now, across three generations — the kind of show that reframes an entire lineage while it's happening; worth the trip to LIC while it's still fresh.

events.name: Elmgreen & Dragset: TRANSITION
events.why: A 40-ton traversable corten steel sculpture — an almost full-scale Oval Office — that you walk through: architecture as power critique, physical space as psychological event; the kind of obsessive, unreasonably literal concept that lands as pure experience.

events.name: Gottlieb / Rothko: The Surrealist Years
events.why: Two New York School titans examined in the specific window before their Abstract Expressionist identities hardened — when they were still fluent in myth, symbols, and automatic image-making; rare chance to see the systems behind the myths.

events.name: Na Mira: NO SMOKING — Opening
events.venue: MoMA, Kravis Studio, Floor 4, 11 W 53rd St, Manhattan
events.why: Na Mira's first solo museum show in New York: a commissioned media installation using radio frequencies, infrared heat, and holography drawn from Korean shamanism and structural filmmaking — it's about how imaging technologies were militarized and how images propagandize at the edge of perception, right in your wheelhouse of hidden systems shaping reality.

events.name: Leonora Carrington & Cecilia Vicuña — Opening
events.why: Historical Surrealist mythmaking (Carrington) in direct dialogue with Vicuña's fiber/language/ecological shamanism — two artists who dissolved boundaries between the human, natural, and imagined, placed in conversation for the first time; mythology as formal method.
